scopeAndContent:
Names of 14,400 Protestant householders for parts of the counties of Londonderry, Donegal, Antrim, Armagh and Tyrone taken from the returns to the Irish House of Commons concerning religion (P.R.O., Dublin bundle 75 of Parliamentary religious returns).
147 pages of typescript.
The coverage of this list is as follows:
Co. Londonderry: Most parishes in the Baronies of Tirkeeran, Kennaght, Coleraine, Loughinsholin.
Co. Antrim: Most parishes in the Baronies of Dunluce, Cary, Kilconway, Toome.
Co. Donegal: Most parishes in the Baronies of Inishowen.
Co. Down: Seapatrick and Kilbroney.
Co. Armagh: Parishes of Shankill, Mullaghbrack, Derrynoose and Tynan.
Co. Tyrone: Parishes of Kildress and Derryloran.
These lists are described as including "all the names of all Protestant Housekeepers in Londonderry Walk under the inspection of Gustavus Henderson supervisor of hearthmoney of Londonderry survey anno 1740.

scopeAndContent:
Handwritten volume 25, of Maxwell Given notes.  

This volume includes pages 5974-6357 of Maxwell Given's notes. These include:  notes relating to Killowen Presbyterian Congregation, 1840-1849; notes relating to Ballylintagh Congregation, 1809-1860; transcripts of the Minutes of the General Assembly of Coleraine Presbytery, 1841; notes relating to the Origin of the Secession Church in Coleraine District; notes relating to the Ballylintagh and Dromore Congregation, 1912, from historical memoirs compiled by Robert Blair of Coleraine; notes on the Secession Church, 1733-1818; notes relating to Coleraine Methodist Church, 1765-1789; a list of the Hearth money roll, 1669, for the parish of Ballymoney; a list of Ballymoney parish poll tax returns, 1660; details relating to abstracts of Wills of the Neilson family of the Conor Diocese, 1627-1724; details relating to the Smith family Wills of the Conor Diocese, 1716-1761; transcripts of the Londonderry muster roll, 1630; notes from the Ordnance Survey Memoir relating to the Parish of Drumachase; list of the Parliamentary Returns relating to Drumachase Parish from the Dublin Record Office, 1766; notes relating to the Plantation of Ulster, 1610; notes relating to Coleraine Dominicans; details relating to the Wills of John Galt, Coleraine Alderman, and his family, 1700-1797; notes relating to the fortifications of Coleraine, 1609-1610; list of gentry and clergy in Limavady, 1839; notes relating to the Coleraine Old Bridge, 1845; notes taken from the 'Post Chaise Companion and Travellers Directory throughout Ireland' by W. Wilson, 1788; transcripts of letters printed in the works of Rev. Dr Jonathan Swift, Dean of St Patrick's, Dublin, 1772; and notes relating to the Bann Fishery, 1542-1799.

User's note:  what has been included here are only the pages 6047 to 6066, and 6095 to 6109. These consist of transcripts of hearth money tax of 1669 for parish of Ballymoney;  poll tax returns 1660; and parliamentary returns re: religious census of 1766 for town of Limavady and parts of parish of Drumachase.

resultInfoList.displayTitle: Hearth money roll for county Donegal, 1665
scopeAndContent:
The original roll — of which TCD MS 6232 is a typescript by Tenison Groves made in the early twentieth century after consulting the original — was held by the Public Record Office of Ireland in the 'Hearth Money Rolls' series within the Vice Treasurer and Auditor General's Office in the Revenue Side of the Exchequer of Ireland. 

This transcript covers the entire county of Donegal. It lists the names of taxpayers by barony (Banagh and Boylagh, Inishowen, Kilmacrenan, Raphoe and Tirhugh), parish, and townland. The roll also records the number of hearths each taxpayer was paying for. Where no number is given, the payment was for one hearth. The roll was compiled under the initial hearth tax legislation (14 & 15 Charles II, c. 17 [1663–4]). This Act did not impose a charge on houses with no hearths, allowing many to legally avoid paying the tax. This Act was replaced by 17 & 18 Charles II, c. 18 (1665–6), which closed off loopholes in the legislation, and allowed for the farming of the tax. Rolls compiled under the amending legislation are typically more complete than earlier rolls. 

The entire roll for Donegal transcribed by Tenison Groves contains 3,508 individual entries (though a small number were obliterated in the original roll, and Groves could not transcribe them). Most households paid for a single hearth, with only 71 paying for multiple hearths, including George Cary (10 hearths), Sir Henry Brooke (10), The Bishop and Dean of Raphoe (10 and 4 respectively), and the Bishop Of Derry (15). Tax was paid for about 3,640 hearths.
